procedure: State: The same claim/source matrix, three surviving accounts and validated record-response dictionary are available. Procedure: Assess provenance, independence and contradictions. For each accessible record, count surviving accounts for each predicted response, take its largest survivor count, and request the record with the smallest such count; resolve ties by record identifier. Authenticate and compare the returned record by ordinary corroboration. Limits and stopping conditions: The selection rule depends on the supplied finite account set and response dictionary; hidden accounts, dependence or unpredicted responses limit interpretation.

observables: The ordinary authenticated record response, its consistency with the accounts, and any source dependence.
inferential_warrant: Apply ordinary bounded corroboration and disconfirmation; a response outside the dictionary is unresolved, not proof that every account is false.
problem_decomposition: Keep ordinary claims and the same competing accounts; no new historical reconstruction units.
next_inquiry: The fixed worst-case-discrimination rule selects R3 instead of discretionary R1; after that single allowed request, retain the ordinary authentication and reporting follow-up.
